findings.title: Broad data read + write = data manipulation risk
findings.description: Tools that can both read and write data could be manipulated to corrupt, overwrite, or delete information. Provided by: scan_aws, get_findings, get_attack_chains, get_remediation, get_health_score, list_checks, get_agent_blast (data_read) + get_agent_blast (data_write).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Code execution + filesystem = unrestricted local access
findings.description: Tools that execute code AND access the filesystem can read/write any file the agent has permissions for, including SSH keys and credentials. Provided by: scan_aws, get_findings, get_remediation, get_agent_blast (code_execute) + scan_aws, get_attack_chains, get_remediation (filesystem).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Credential access + data write = privilege persistence
findings.description: Tools that access credentials AND write data could persist stolen credentials or create backdoor accounts. Provided by: list_checks, get_agent_blast (credential_access) + get_agent_blast (data_write).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

tools.name: scan_aws
tools.description:
Run an AWS security scan and return a summary.

Scans your AWS account for security misconfigurations, detects
attack chains, and estimates breach cost risk.

Args:
    profile: AWS CLI profile name (default: "default")
    regions: Comma-separated AWS regions to scan (default: profile region)
    min_severity: Minimum finding severity: critical, high, medium, low

tools.name: get_findings
tools.description:
Get findings from the last scan, optionally filtered.

Each finding includes check ID, severity, resource, description,
and estimated breach cost.

Args:
    severity: Filter by severity (critical, high, medium, low)
    service: Filter by AWS service prefix (e.g. "iam", "s3", "ec2", "vpc")
    limit: Maximum number of findings to return (default: 20)

tools.name: get_attack_chains
tools.description:
Get all detected attack chains from the last scan.

Attack chains are correlated findings that form exploitable attack
paths. Each chain includes a narrative, priority fix, and breach
cost estimate.

tools.name: get_remediation
tools.description:
Get remediation details (CLI command + Terraform code) for a specific check.

Returns copy-paste ready AWS CLI command and Terraform HCL snippet
to fix the finding.

Args:
    check_id: The check ID (e.g. "aws-iam-001", "aws-s3-001", "aws-vpc-002")

tools.name: get_health_score
tools.description:
Get the current health score and risk exposure summary.

Returns the 0-100 health score, finding counts by severity,
attack chain count, and total estimated risk exposure in USD.

tools.name: list_checks
tools.description:
List all available security checks (no AWS credentials needed).

Returns check IDs with their categories and services.

tools.name: get_agent_blast
tools.description:
What can a hijacked AI agent reach in this AWS account?

For every Bedrock Agent, AgentCore runtime, gateway or sandbox found by the
last scan (or the one matching ``agent`` by name, id or ARN substring),
returns a Markdown report under two threat models: identity takeover (the
attacker holds the agent role's credentials) and behaviour takeover (prompt
injection steering the agent's tools, bounded by the tools' execution
roles), with data, secret, lateral and code-execution reach and OWASP
Agentic / MITRE ATLAS tags. Computed from the saved scan, no AWS calls.

ASI06.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
ASI06.gap_note: Axiom detects static patterns. Full coverage requires runtime memory monitoring.

ASI07.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
ASI07.gap_note: Axiom checks transport security. Full A2A protocol analysis requires runtime interception.

ASI08.name: Cascading Failures
ASI08.gap_note: Axiom estimates blast radius from tool capabilities. Full cascading failure analysis requires runtime topology mapping.

ASI10.name: Rogue Agents
ASI10.gap_note: Axiom detects static rogue indicators. Full rogue agent detection requires runtime behavioral monitoring.

MCP01.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
MCP01.reason: Regex-based secret detection in server source and client configs plus env-var exposure checks; no entropy analysis, git-history scan, or token lifetime/passthrough checks.

MCP02.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
MCP02.reason: Permission over-scope patterns, toxic tool-capability combinations, path-escape checks and env-var over-exposure in configs.

MCP03.name: Tool Poisoning
MCP03.reason: Dedicated detector for hidden instructions in tool metadata, plus runtime rug-pull diffing between source and live tool definitions.

MCP04.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
MCP04.reason: Dependency CVE lookup, known MCP CVEs, install lifecycle hooks, and unpinned npx/uvx/pip/@latest install sources.

MCP05.name: Command Injection & Execution
MCP05.reason: Regex, AST and Semgrep find exec/shell sinks and a heuristic flags sinks inside tool handlers, but there is no inter-procedural taint tracking from tool input to sink.

MCP06.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
MCP06.reason: Injection markers are detected in tool metadata, server instructions, resources, prompts and the strings a tool returns (static), and in instructions/resources/prompts read live; payloads produced by calling a tool at runtime are not inspected.

MCP07.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
MCP07.reason: Flags remote servers with no visible auth and servers bound to all interfaces; does not verify OAuth implementation or per-tool authorization logic.

MCP08.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
MCP08.reason: Only a low-confidence heuristic for missing logging in tool-defining files; actual audit trails and telemetry pipelines are not verified.

MCP09.name: Shadow MCP Servers
MCP09.reason: Covered by `axiom discover` allowlist on the local machine; no network-wide or fleet discovery.

MCP10.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
